concepts.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: an original tiny digital companion mascot for a modern learning app used by children and teenagers, appealing equally to adults. A neutral cool technology-oriented desktop pet, an ambient little presence in the corner of a screen. Contemporary restrained industrial design crossed with a collectible digital character. Friendly but not sugary or babyish. Express personality almost entirely through simple eyes, tilt and pose. No mathematical symbols, fractions, belly circles, circular charge gauges, antennae, clothing, human features, fur, ears, tails, backpacks, or props. No famous franchise resemblance, no branding. Color palette: warm light gray backdrop #F3F4F1, charcoal #20292D, emerald #1E7358, a restrained luminous pale mint #B8F4D3 highlight. Keep all forms bold and simple, very legible as a 32px desktop companion. Premium product presentation with generous negative space, beautifully controlled silhouette. No text, no numbers, no captions, no watermark. Landscape character design board: one large three-quarter full-body neutral pose on the left, and on the right two smaller poses of EXACTLY THE SAME character, curious tilted and quietly happy. Clean simple backdrop, faint contact shadow only, no scenery. Concept BIT: a sophisticated pixel-art digital sprite. True crisply aligned pixel art, no smooth curves, no painterly brushwork, no blurry edges. Small chunky oblong charcoal creature with stepped beveled corners, like an irregular eight-bit computer tile, width slightly more than height, NOT a perfect cube. One corner has a distinctive two-step notch. Two luminous mint horizontal rectangular eyes, set low and wide, no mouth. Just two very short stepped feet and two tiny side pixels for hands, keeping an extremely clean non-animal silhouette. Two small emerald pixel blocks on one flank. Limited flat palette, minimal 1px highlights, stylish and deadpan personality. No retro game references, no surrounding decorative pixel motifs. Make the face feel observant and quietly alive.

revision.prompt:
Edit the provided reference image of the charcoal pixel-art desktop pet. Preserve its appealing original compact stepped silhouette, wide rounded-oblong pixel body, two tiny side hands, two tiny feet, widely spaced simple rectangular eyes, and the three-pose presentation: large neutral figure on the left, curious tilt top right, happy eyes bottom right. This is a restrained refinement of this exact character, not a redesign into a different creature.
Make the character much lighter, more welcoming for an educational entertainment app. Replace the black charcoal body with warm ivory and very pale mint, with tasteful muted emerald outlines and pale celadon stepped shading. The face is the same light body surface, NO black face screen. Eyes are dark forest green rectangular pixel eyes, very clear against the light face. The two small existing side accent pixels are sunny apricot yellow. Backdrop is plain warm off-white, with subtle small pixel-art ground shadows.
Add ONE clever recognizable distinguishing feature: a single little square golden-yellow detachable "companion pixel", hovering just above and beside the upper-right corner of the body. The upper-right body corner has a clearly matching one-square stepped notch where this pixel belongs, visually like one pixel gently broke away and came to life. This tiny satellite pixel is about the width of ONE eye, not a big cube, has no face, no trail, no sparkles, and never looks like an antenna or a hat. In the curious pose it hovers beside the direction of the gaze; in the happy pose it floats slightly higher. The sprite remains extremely simple and distinctive. Keep the asymmetrical notch consistent across all three poses. Only one floating pixel per pose.
Style: crisp high-quality aligned pixel art with clean square corners; limited palette, intentional pixel clusters, subtle 2-tone depth only, preserve the reference style without metallic reflections, no furry rendering, no glossy 3D plastic. The palette should feel fresh, bright, calm and playful, sophisticated for ages 10–16. Keep the neutral face observant and a little mischievous, the tilted face curious and the happy face with simple inverted-U pixel eyes. All limbs fully inside frame, generous whitespace. No text, numbers, captions, logos, arithmetic, fractions, belly icons, circles or badges. Do not add mouth, ears, tail, antenna, costumes or extra appendages.
